item.title: Correction · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: The summary for UCSF Mission Bay Housing…
item.description: The summary for UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building now includes SFGate's May 31, 2009 report on the campus. Source: https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php.

item.title: Correction · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building page…
item.description: UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building page now says that sources differ on how many people the four-building housing complex holds (Langan: more than 750 students, postdoctoral scholars and their families; the 2002 UC Regents plan: 717 students and postdoctoral scholars and the family of one manager; arcCA Digest: a 760-bed complex) and on its architect (arcCA Digest: SOM with Fisher Friedman; Langan: Verde Design, Inc.). The timeline date of May 31, 2009 is the date of an SFGate article saying the campus then had four residential buildings, not an opening date; the 2002 Regents item expected full occupancy by October 2005. The footprint is described as crowd-mapped OpenStreetMap data, not a survey. Source: https://www.langan.com/portfolio/ucsf-mission-bay-student-housing; https://arccadigest.org/uc-san-francisco-dna-campus/; https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/minutes/2002/gbf1102.pdf; https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php.

Source: https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php; https://arccadigest.org/uc-san-francisco-dna-campus/; https://www.langan.com/portfolio/ucsf-mission-bay-student-housing; https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/minutes/2002/gbf1102.pdf.

item.title: Correction · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: The four UCSF Block 20 housing buildings…
item.description: The four UCSF Block 20 housing buildings showed an October 2005 opening that was only ever a 2002 forecast. Their completion now rests on SFGate's May 2009 report that the campus had four residential buildings, so they were complete by then; the actual opening date is still not confirmed. Source: https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php.

item.title: Correction · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: The record no longer says the building…
item.description: The record no longer says the building opened around 2005 or in June 2005: no source read gives an opening date (Langan gives none and UCSF's housing page could not be read), so the milestone now carries the October 2005 full occupancy that the November 2002 Regents item anticipated, marked expected. The Regents approval is described as the committees approving and forwarding to the Board. Use now reads student, postdoctoral scholar and family housing (Langan, Regents) instead of student and faculty, the facts about the four-building complex cite Langan, the example of a parcel spanning several UCSF buildings now says about 12.2 acres at 675 Mission Bay Blvd, the SOM architect attribution cites arcCA Digest, and the aerial photo's caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'. Source: UC Regents committee minutes, 2002-11-13 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/minutes/2002/gbf1102.pdf); Langan, UCSF Mission Bay Student Housing (https://www.langan.com/portfolio/ucsf-mission-bay-student-housing); arcCA Digest, UC San Francisco: The DNA of a Campus (https://arccadigest.org/uc-san-francisco-dna-campus/); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sfgov.org/Geographic-Locations-and-Boundaries/Parcels-Active-and-Retired/acdm-wktn).

item.title: Added · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: The November 2002 UC Regents budget of…
item.description: The November 2002 UC Regents budget of $112,816,000 covers the whole Block 20 project (Hearst Tower plus the Housing North, Housing West and Student Housing buildings) with no per-building breakdown, so it is not a cost for Housing North alone. It is now listed once in the shared site-wide cost list for Mission Bay, and this record points to it. Source: UC Regents Committees on Grounds and Buildings and on Finance, joint meeting minutes, 2002-11-13 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/minutes/2002/gbf1102.pdf).

item.title: Complete · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: SFGate's May 31, 2009 article on… (~May 2009)
item.description: SFGate's May 31, 2009 article on the Helen Diller building says "With the opening of the Diller building at 1450 Third St., the Mission Bay campus now has four research buildings, a community center and four residential buildings." The article does not name Block 20 or this housing complex, so reading its four residential buildings as the four-building Block 20 complex is an inference. May 31, 2009 is the article's publication date, not an opening date: it shows the complex was open by then, and no source read gives the date it actually opened (the November 2002 Regents item had anticipated full occupancy by October 2005) (~May 2009). Source: SFGate, 2009-05-31.

item.title: Complete · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: UCSF Mission Bay Housing North… (~May 2009)
item.description: UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: no source gives its opening date. SFGate, published May 31, 2009 (the date shown is the article's date, not an opening date), said the Mission Bay campus 'now has four research buildings, a community center and four residential buildings' without naming them; this building is one of the four buildings of UCSF's Block 20 housing complex, so it is presumably among them. The November 13, 2002 UC Regents item anticipated full occupancy of the complex by October 2005 (an expected date, not an event) (~May 2009). Source: https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php ; https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/minutes/2002/gbf1102.pdf.

item.title: Planned · UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building: UC Regents' Grounds and… (Nov 13, 2002)
item.description: UC Regents' Grounds and Buildings and Finance committees approve, and vote to present to the Board, a $112,816,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Block 20 Housing and Retail Project – one 15-story tower and three mid-rise buildings around a shared courtyard, 298,800 residential asf and 430 apartment units total – with construction to begin June 2003 and full occupancy anticipated by October 2005 (Nov 13, 2002). Source: The Regents of the University of California, 2002-11.
item.source: The Regents of the University of California, 2002-11
